title: `navigation.activation` can have a null `entry` when entries and events are disabled [zcorpan/navigation-api-qa]

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
*[Update document for history step application](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#update-document-for-history-step-application)* step 7 sets up `navigation`'s activation whenever *previousEntryForActivation* is given and *navigationType* is non-null, without checking whether `navigation` [has entries and events disabled](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#has-entries-and-events-disabled). Step 7.5 then says:

> Set *activation*'s new entry to *navigation*'s current entry.

and [current entry](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigation-current-entry) says:

> If *navigation* has entries and events disabled, then return null.

So in an opaque-origin document reached by a traversal or reload, `navigation.activation` returns an object whose non-nullable `entry` has nothing valid to return.

[Test case](https://github.com/zcorpan/navigation-api-qa/blob/6394f99fb120977f139a718c15960d3672e19ac1/findings/01-gecko-activation-entry-null-crash/test.html): a sandboxed iframe (`allow-scripts` only) loads a `data:` document and navigates to a second `data:` document, which calls `history.back()`. The first document is recreated and reads `navigation.activation.entry`. Chrome Canary and Safari TP return null from `navigation.activation` there; Chromium's getter checks for entries and events disabled ([navigation_api.cc](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/6ca4e60b94475fa916dfb688608e6cc72693a1bf/third_party/blink/renderer/core/navigation_api/navigation_api.cc#110)). Firefox Nightly follows the spec text, and reading `entry` crashes its content process.

(Found in https://github.com/zcorpan/navigation-api-qa.)
